documents.title: Tomato field demonstrations and blight context

passages.text: An ICAR-KVK Dehradun field demonstration associated closely planted tomato canopies and limited ventilation with higher humidity and more early- and late-blight problems. The demonstration reported better results when spacing and canopy management were improved. These observations are specific to that region and trial; they are not a diagnosis or a universal spray recommendation. Ask the local KVK about suitable spacing and disease management for the variety and season grown in your area.

documents.title: Potato late blight and its management

passages.text: ICAR describes potato late blight as starting on leaves with pale green, water-soaked spots, often near leaf margins and tips. In moist conditions the spots may enlarge and become dark or necrotic; affected stems and tubers may also show symptoms. Similar-looking damage can have other causes, so these signs alone do not confirm late blight. Inspect plants regularly and request local plant-pathology or KVK confirmation when symptoms spread quickly.

ICAR's 2025 Kharif advisory includes maize disease-management guidance and discusses action when rust symptoms are observed. Crop-protection recommendations in an advisory depend on its region, season, product label and current local rules. Identify the crop and symptoms first, and confirm any treatment with a local KVK or agricultural officer; this local knowledge entry intentionally gives no pesticide dose or product schedule.

passages.section: Grape — black rot symptoms and sanitation
passages.text: MANAGE's agricultural extension study material describes grape black rot symptoms on leaves as irregular reddish-brown spots that can contain small black fruiting structures; affected berries may become dark, shrivelled and mummy-like. Remove and safely dispose of diseased plant parts and mummified berries as part of vineyard sanitation. Visual symptoms are not enough to confirm a disease, and this reference does not provide a location-specific treatment schedule.

documents.title: Integrated Pest Management: A Sustainable Approach to Responsible Pest Management
documents.publisher: ICAR Research Complex for North Eastern Hill Region

passages.text: ICAR presents integrated pest management as a combination of prevention, regular monitoring and informed decisions. It prioritizes suitable non-chemical, cultural, physical, biological and varietal measures, using pesticides only when needed and according to the product label and an appropriate local recommendation. A general chatbot result should not replace diagnosis or label directions.

passages.section: Soil health and balanced nutrient management
passages.text: ICAR-CPRI's farmer-awareness programme highlights soil testing, balanced nutrient management, water conservation and locally suitable agricultural guidance. Fertilizer requirements vary with the crop, field, soil test, season and region. Use a current soil test and recommendations from the relevant local agricultural authority; this knowledge base does not estimate or prescribe fertilizer quantities.
